question: An otherwise eligible family moves permanently from another Canadian province to Alberta on May 18, registers promptly for AHCIP, and has no special exemption. When does Alberta coverage ordinarily start, and what should the family do during the waiting period?
generated_answer:
According to the Alberta Health Care Insurance Plan (AHCIP) rules, when a family moves to Alberta from another Canadian province, they are subject to a waiting period before their Alberta coverage starts.

The waiting period is typically 3 months from the date of arrival in Alberta. Since the family arrived on May 18, their waiting period would end on August 17.

Ordinarily, Alberta coverage would start on August 18, which is the first day after the 3-month waiting period.

During the waiting period, the family should maintain their out-of-province health insurance coverage, if they have it. If they don't have out-of-province coverage, they may want to consider purchasing private health insurance to cover any unexpected medical expenses that may arise during the waiting period.

It's also a good idea for the family to register with a primary care physician or a medical clinic in Alberta, even if they're not yet covered under AHCIP, so they can receive medical attention if needed. However, they would need to pay out-of-pocket for any medical services received during the waiting period, unless they have private insurance that covers these expenses.

Once their Alberta coverage starts on August 18, the family can access publicly funded healthcare services, including doctor visits, hospital stays, and other medical services, without having to pay out-of-pocket.
